{"triples": [{"subject": "classifier", "predicate": "uses", "object": "embeddings", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Train the probe on the embeddings as input"}, {"subject": "Evaluation", "predicate": "uses", "object": "embeddings", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Usually, the evaluation score from step 6 is used as a basis to make inferences regarding the presence of the probed information in embeddings"}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "Experiments", "predicate": "uses", "object": "10 established probing task datasets", "object_type": "Dataset", "source_sentence": "In our experiments we use 10 established probing task datasets for the English language introduced by Conneau et al."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "sub-word tokens", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "While BERT uses sub-word tokens to get around out of vocabulary tokens, in the rare instance of encountering an OOV with GloVe, we generate a random word embedding in its stead."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "random word embedding", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "While BERT uses sub-word tokens to get around out of vocabulary tokens, in the rare instance of encountering an OOV with GloVe, we generate a random word embedding in its stead."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "sentence embeddings", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Finally, we use the vanilla BERT and GloVe sentence embeddings in their respective evaluations as vanilla baselines against which the models with noise are compared."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "sentence embeddings", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Finally, we use the vanilla BERT and GloVe sentence embeddings in their respective evaluations as vanilla baselines against which the models with noise are compared."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "comparesAgainst", "object": "random baselines", "object_type": "Model", "source_sentence": "The vanilla GloVe vectors outperform the random baselines on all tasks except BS."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "addresses", "object": "local-context task", "object_type": "Task", "source_sentence": "This is not surprising, as BS is essentially a local-context task, and GloVe does not encode context in such a localised manner."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "specifically BERT stores information pertinent to the BS, SOMO and TC tasks in the norm"}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "while GloVe uses it to store SL, WC, TC and TD information"}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "achieves", "object": "out-perform random baselines across all tasks", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "The vanilla BERT vectors out- perform random baselines across all tasks, includ- ing the BS task."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "vector norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "Given that we know that BERT is a contextual encoder, and that its self-attention uses the vector norm to control the levels of contribution from less informative words"}, {"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "BERT is evidently capable of encoding this signal well, and seems to be using its norm to supplement the encoding of the phenomenon in such a way that it positions sentences exhibiting local contextual incongruity closer to the origin, relative to sentences that do not contain it."}, {"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "Furthermore, BERT's ability to model incongruity via the norm could essentially be frequency-based, similar to how some word embeddings encode word frequency in the norm."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "In contrast, GloVe is a static encoder and exhibits no indication that it stores this information in the norm, or indeed any ability to accurately model this phenomenon at all, but uses the norm to store surface-level and syntactic information."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "GloVe uses the norm to encode sentence length, as reflected in our experiments in §4."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Our findings show that BERT primarily uses the norm to store contextual incongruity information and positions incongruous sentences closer to the origin."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Meanwhile, GloVe stores much more syntactic information in its norm than BERT, but does not store contextual information at all, and mainly stores surface-level information in the norm."}]}
